A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VeriTrail study. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments, ablations, annotation analyses, and error-stage statistics on FABLES+ and DiverseSumm+.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds MiniCheck evaluations and measurements of the proportion of graph nodes verified.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the Appendix C prompts are unchanged. Claim decomposition, evidence selection, verdict generation, reverse traversal, and q-based termination are retained. The rewritten method description and discussion of alternative verifiers do not establish an implemented procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate hierarchical summarization on FABLES+ and GraphRAG on DiverseSumm+, retaining 22 books with 734 claims and 20 questions with 560 claims, respectively. The 415-claim supplementary subset is also unchanged. No additional dataset, domain, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds the baseline labeled Llama-3.1-Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B to the hard and soft prediction comparisons. AlignScore, INFUSE, RAG, the long-context models, and the VT-RAG ablation comparator remain.

E3.justification: The new MiniCheck evaluation uses approximately 32K-token chunks, top-k aggregation over k=1–5 for FABLES+ and k=1–15 for DiverseSumm+, and thresholds 0.5–0.9. Table 1 changes AlignScore's selected DiverseSumm+ configuration from k=2, threshold 0.5 to k=1, threshold 0.9. Existing datasets, metrics, and other principal protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix D adds an efficiency analysis measuring node-verification fractions at q=1 and q=3, and Figure 4 adds MiniCheck hyperparameter sensitivity results. The component ablation moves from v1 Section 5 to v2 Appendix E.1; existing input-limit, prompt, termination, model, error-case, and error-stage analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three sampled outputs at temperature 0.2 for confidence estimation, annotation-agreement statistics, and 1,000 bootstrap resamples with 95% confidence intervals for error-stage attribution. No changed seed information, repetition counts, or uncertainty-reporting procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Baseline and cost evidence is substantially revised. AlignScore's DiverseSumm+ macro F1 changes from 42.7 to 60.4 under different selected configurations, and its soft AUROC changes from 0.35 to 0.68. MiniCheck scores and node-verification fractions are added. Several cost estimates change substantially, including DiverseSumm+ RAG at k=15 from $0.25 to $0.04 per claim. VeriTrail's main accuracy results and existing ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds a stated worst-case O(|V|) per-claim time-complexity bound, explained through visiting all graph nodes. The DAG definitions, error-stage definitions, and error-attribution equations are retained; no new theorem or formal proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The principal traceability, dataset, and detection-performance contributions remain. v2 explicitly promotes cost-effectiveness into the introduction's contribution list and the conclusion, while dropping the earlier concluding emphasis on user control over the cost/conservatism tradeoff.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix G newly discusses replacing Verdict Generation with alternative verifiers. Conversely, it removes v1 Section 3.3's explicit explanation of how smaller q can increase false positives, including the possibility that supported information disappears and later reappears in intermediate outputs. The original error-case interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds MiniCheck access, model, A100 hardware, and 20-hour runtime details; explicitly describes parallel evidence-selection prompts; and clarifies RAG embedding-cost amortization. It removes the earlier 64-core/256-GiB host specification. Dataset release remains prospective, and the new reproducibility section mainly points to existing documentation.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially into open- versus closed-domain and reference-free versus reference-based detection, including arguments about model access and applicability to existing outputs. Added works include Lookback Lens, ReDeEP, FEQA, QuestEval, G-Eval, ARES, and MiniCheck. The earlier DAG and reasoning-chain comparisons are retained.

P1.justification: The central exposition is substantially reorganized: verification becomes named subsections, verdict definitions move into the conceptual framework, and design-feature explanations are distributed between the method and cost appendix. The main-text ablation moves to Appendix E.1, related work is expanded, a reproducibility section is added, and the Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is restyled and relabeled, existing plots receive title and axis-label edits, and a MiniCheck heatmap and comparison-table rows are added. The ablation and cost tables are relocated. The document adopts ICLR headers and typography while retaining the principal table and chart formats.

improvement.justification: The added MiniCheck comparisons, clearer method exposition, broader research positioning, and expanded cost accounting provide a modest net improvement. These gains are tempered by removal of the explicit q/false-positive tradeoff discussion. Also, the retained statement that all VeriTrail variants outperform the baselines is not established at the reported precision in v2 Table 5, where MiniCheck and VeriTrail t=1 both have 0.79 AUROC on DiverseSumm+.
